title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 1:1
body: “The beginning of the book promises blessing to him that reads and hears and keeps, that he who takes pains about the reading may thence learn to do works, and may keep the precepts.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 1:1
bodyEs: “El principio del libro promete bendición al que lee, y oye, y guarda, para que el que se toma el trabajo de la lectura aprenda de ahí a hacer obras, y guarde los preceptos.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 1:4
body: “He is, because He endures continually; He was, because with the Father He made all things, and has at this time taken a beginning from the Virgin; He is to come, because assuredly He will come to judgment.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 1:4
bodyEs: “Él es, porque permanece de continuo; él era, porque con el Padre hizo todas las cosas, y en este tiempo ha tomado un principio de la Virgen; ha de venir, porque ciertamente vendrá al juicio.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 2:2
body: “In the first epistle He speaks thus: I know that thou sufferest and workest, I see that thou art patient; think not that I am staying long from thee.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 2:2
bodyEs: “En la primera epístola habla así: Sé que sufres y trabajas, veo que eres paciente; no pienses que me quedo mucho tiempo lejos de ti.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 2:6
body: “But because thou thyself hatest those who hold the doctrines of the Nicolaitanes, thou expectest praise. Moreover, to hate the works of the Nicolaitanes, which He Himself also hated, this tends to praise.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 2:6
bodyEs: “Pero porque tú mismo aborreces a los que sostienen las doctrinas de los nicolaítas, esperas alabanza. Además, aborrecer las obras de los nicolaítas, las cuales él mismo también aborreció, esto tiende a la alabanza.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 3:2
body: “For it is not enough for a tree to live and to have no fruit, even as it is not enough to be called a Christian and to confess Christ, but not to have Himself in our work, that is, not to do His precepts.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 3:2
bodyEs: “Porque no basta que un árbol viva y no tenga fruto, así como no basta ser llamado cristiano y confesar a Cristo, pero no tenerlo a él en nuestra obra, esto es, no hacer sus preceptos.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 3:10
body: “That they may know His glory to be of this kind, that they are not indeed permitted to be given over to temptation.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 3:10
bodyEs: “Para que conozcan que su gloria es de esta clase: que no se les permite, en verdad, ser entregados a la tentación.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 4:2
body: “And since the mind of the faithful is opened by the Holy Spirit, and that is manifested to them which was also foretold to the fathers, he distinctly says:--”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 4:2
bodyEs: “Y puesto que la mente de los fieles es abierta por el Espíritu Santo, y se les manifiesta lo que también fue anunciado a los padres, dice con claridad:”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 4:3
body: “Upon the throne he says that he saw the likeness of a jasper and a sardine stone. The jasper is of the colour of water, the sardine of fire.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 4:3
bodyEs: “Sobre el trono dice que vio la semejanza de una piedra de jaspe y de sardio. El jaspe es del color del agua, el sardio del fuego.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 5:1
body: “This book signifies the Old Testament, which has been given into the hands of our Lord Jesus Christ, who received from the Father judgment.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 5:1
bodyEs: “Este libro significa el Antiguo Testamento, que ha sido entregado en las manos de nuestro Señor Jesucristo, quien recibió del Padre el juicio.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 5:4
body: “Neither among the angels of heaven, nor among men in earth, nor among the souls of the saints in rest, save Christ the Son of God alone, whom he says that he saw as a Lamb standing as it were slain, having seven horns. What had not been then announced, and what the law had contemplated for Him by its various oblations and sacrifices, it behoved Himself to fulfil.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 5:4
bodyEs: “Ni entre los ángeles del cielo, ni entre los hombres en la tierra, ni entre las almas de los santos en el descanso, sino solo Cristo, el Hijo de Dios, de quien dice que lo vio como un Cordero en pie, como inmolado, que tenía siete cuernos. Lo que entonces no se había anunciado, y lo que la ley había contemplado para él por sus diversas ofrendas y sacrificios, le correspondía a él mismo cumplirlo.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 6:5
body: “The black horse signifies famine, for the Lord says, "There shall be famines in divers places;" but the word is specially extended to the times of Antichrist, when there shall be a great famine, and when all shall be injured. Moreover, the balance in the hand is the examining scales, wherein He might show forth the merits of every individual.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 6:5
bodyEs: “El caballo negro significa hambre, porque el Señor dice: «habrá hambres … por los lugares»; pero la palabra se extiende de modo especial a los tiempos del Anticristo, cuando habrá una gran hambre, y cuando todos serán dañados. Además, la balanza en la mano son las balanzas de examen, en las cuales podría mostrar los méritos de cada persona.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 6:6
body: “That is, strike not the spiritual man with thy inflictions. This is the black horse.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 6:6
bodyEs: “Esto es, no hieras con tus azotes al hombre espiritual. Este es el caballo negro.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 7:2
body: “He speaks of Elias the prophet, who is the precursor of the times of Antichrist, for the restoration and establishment of the churches from the great and intolerable persecution.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 7:2
bodyEs: “Habla de Elías el profeta, que es el precursor de los tiempos del Anticristo, para la restauración y el establecimiento de las iglesias después de la persecución grande e intolerable.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 7:9
body: “What the great multitude out of every tribe implies, is to show the number of the elect out of all believers, who, being cleansed by baptism in the blood of the Lamb, have made their robes white, keeping the grace which they have received.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 7:9
bodyEs: “Lo que implica la gran multitud de toda tribu es mostrar el número de los elegidos de entre todos los creyentes, que, limpiados por el bautismo en la sangre del Cordero, han blanqueado sus vestiduras, guardando la gracia que han recibido.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 8:1
body: “Whereby is signified the beginning of everlasting rest; but it is described as partial, because the silence being interrupted, he repeats it in order. For if the silence had continued, here would be an end of his narrative.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 8:1
bodyEs: “Con lo cual se significa el principio del descanso eterno; pero se describe como parcial, porque, interrumpido el silencio, lo repite en orden. Porque si el silencio hubiera continuado, aquí habría un fin de su narración.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 8:13
body: “By the angel flying through the midst of heaven is signified the Holy Spirit bearing witness in two of the prophets that a great wrath of plagues was imminent. If by any means, even in the last times, any one should be willing to be converted, any one might even still be saved.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 8:13
bodyEs: “Por el ángel que vuela por en medio del cielo se significa el Espíritu Santo dando testimonio en dos de los profetas de que una gran ira de plagas era inminente. Si de algún modo, aun en los últimos tiempos, alguno quisiera convertirse, todavía podría salvarse.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 10:3
body: “After them there is now given to the same completed Churches the comfort of having the prophetic Scriptures subsequently interpreted, for I said that after the apostles there would be interpreting prophets.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 10:3
bodyEs: “Después de ellos se da ahora a las mismas Iglesias ya completas el consuelo de tener las Escrituras proféticas interpretadas después, porque dije que después de los apóstoles habría profetas que interpretan.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 10:10
body: “To take the book and eat it up, is, when exhibition of a thing is made to one, to commit it to memory.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 10:10
bodyEs: “Tomar el libro y comerlo es, cuando se le muestra a uno una cosa, confiarla a la memoria.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 11:1
body: “A reed was shown like to a rod. This itself is the Apocalypse which he subsequently exhibited to the churches; for the Gospel of the complete faith he subsequently wrote for the sake of our salvation.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 11:1
bodyEs: “Se mostró una caña semejante a una vara. Esto mismo es el Apocalipsis que después exhibió a las iglesias; porque el Evangelio de la fe completa lo escribió después por causa de nuestra salvación.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 11:2
body: “The space which is called the court is the empty altar within the walls: these being such as were not necessary, he commanded to be ejected from the Church.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 11:2
bodyEs: “El espacio que se llama el atrio es el altar vacío dentro de los muros: siendo estos tales que no eran necesarios, mandó que fueran echados de la Iglesia.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 12:1
body: “The woman clothed with the sun, and having the moon under her feet, and wearing a crown of twelve stars upon her head, and travailing in her pains, is the ancient Church of fathers, and prophets, and saints, and apostles, which had the groans and torments of its longing until it saw that Christ, the fruit of its people according to the flesh long promised to it, had taken flesh out of the selfsame people.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 12:1
bodyEs: “La mujer vestida del sol, y con la luna debajo de sus pies, y que lleva una corona de doce estrellas sobre su cabeza, y que está de parto en sus dolores, es la Iglesia antigua de padres, y profetas, y santos, y apóstoles, que tuvo los gemidos y tormentos de su anhelo hasta que vio que Cristo, el fruto de su pueblo según la carne prometido desde hacía mucho, había tomado carne de ese mismo pueblo.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 12:3
body: “Now, that he says that this dragon was of a red colour--that is, of a purple colour--the result of his work gave him such a colour. For from the beginning (as the Lord says) he was a murderer; and he has oppressed the whole of the human race, not so much by the obligation of death, as, moreover, by the various forms of destruction and fatal mischiefs.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 12:3
bodyEs: “Ahora bien, que dice que este dragón era de color rojo —esto es, de color púrpura—, el resultado de su obra le dio tal color. Porque desde el principio (como dice el Señor) «homicida ha sido»; y ha oprimido a todo el género humano, no tanto por la obligación de la muerte, como, además, por las diversas formas de destrucción y de daños fatales.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 14:6
body: “The angel flying through the midst of heaven, whom he says that he saw, we have already treated of above, as being the same Elias who anticipates the kingdom of Antichrist in his prophecy.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 14:6
bodyEs: “El ángel que vuela por en medio del cielo, del cual dice que lo vio, ya lo hemos tratado arriba, como siendo el mismo Elías que se anticipa al reino del Anticristo en su profecía.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 14:8
body: “The other angel following, he speaks of as the same prophet who is the associate of his prophesying. But that he says,--”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 14:8
bodyEs: “Del otro ángel que sigue, habla como del mismo profeta que es el compañero de su profetizar. Pero que dice:”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 15:1
body: “For the wrath of God always strikes the obstinate people with seven plagues, that is, perfectly, as it is said in Leviticus; and these shall be in the last time, when the Church shall have gone out of the midst.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 15:1
bodyEs: “Porque la ira de Dios hiere siempre al pueblo obstinado con siete plagas, esto es, perfectamente, como se dice en Levítico; y estas serán en el último tiempo, cuando la Iglesia haya salido de en medio.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 15:2
body: “That is, that they stood stedfastly in the faith upon their baptism, and having their confession in their mouth, that they shall exult in the kingdom before God. But let us return to what is set before us.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 15:2
bodyEs: “Esto es, que estuvieron firmes en la fe sobre su bautismo, y teniendo su confesión en la boca, que se regocijarán en el reino delante de Dios. Pero volvamos a lo que se nos pone delante.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 17:3
body: “But to sit upon the scarlet beast, the author of murders, is the image of the devil. Where also is treated of his captivity, concerning which we have fully considered.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 17:3
bodyEs: “Pero sentarse sobre la bestia escarlata, autora de homicidios, es la imagen del diablo. Donde también se trata de su cautiverio, acerca del cual hemos considerado plenamente.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 17:10
body: “The time must be understood in which the written Apocalypse was published, since then reigned Cæsar Domitian; but before him had been Titus his brother, and Vespasian, Otho, Vitellius, and Galba. These are the five who have fallen.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 17:10
bodyEs: “El tiempo ha de entenderse como aquel en que se publicó el Apocalipsis escrito, pues entonces reinaba el César Domiciano; pero antes de él habían estado Tito su hermano, y Vespasiano, Otón, Vitelio y Galba. Estos son los cinco que han caído.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 19:11
body: “The horse, and He that sits upon him, sets forth our Lord coming to His kingdom with the heavenly army. Because from the sea of the north, which is the Arabian Sea, even to the sea of Phoenice, and even to the ends of the earth, they will command these greater parts in the coming of the Lord Jesus, and all the souls of the nations will be assembled to judgment.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 19:11
bodyEs: “El caballo, y el que se sienta sobre él, presentan a nuestro Señor que viene a su reino con el ejército celestial. Porque desde el mar del norte, que es el mar Arábigo, hasta el mar de Fenicia, y hasta los confines de la tierra, mandarán estas partes mayores en la venida del Señor Jesús, y todas las almas de las naciones serán reunidas para el juicio.”

title: Victorinus of Pettau on Revelation 20:6
body: “I do not think the reign of a thousand years is eternal; or if it is thus to be thought of, they cease to reign when the thousand years are finished. But I will put forward what my capacity enables me to judge.”
author: Victorinus of Pettau, Commentary on the Apocalypse, on Revelation 20:6
bodyEs: “No pienso que el reino de mil años sea eterno; o, si ha de pensarse así, dejan de reinar cuando se acaban los mil años. Pero pondré por delante lo que mi capacidad me permite juzgar.”
